ops.title: scripts/fleet-build.sh has no automated coverage, while five other suites drive shell scripts
ops.description:
Split out of `5a3ec1f1` when that task's three acceptance criteria were met and closed (2026-08-30). This was the fourth finding in its body and never had criteria of its own.

`scripts/fleet-build.sh` is 500 lines of awk-heavy parsing that gates every daemonkit release, and nothing tests it. `ci/mixedera/gate_test.go` is the ready template — five other suites in this repo already drive shell scripts from Go.

**Why this is not hypothetical.** Two parser defects were found by review rather than by a test, and one of them shipped and stayed:

- `fleet_requires` decided a `replace (` block had opened by comparing the line's LAST field to `(`, so `replace ( // pin the local tree` left the flag unset and printed every module in the block body as a requirement — putting a peer nobody asked for into a leg's cone. Filed 2026-08-01, fixed 2026-08-30 in `6b64e80`, after a hand-crafted `go.mod` reproduced it. A fixture test would have caught it the day it was written.
- The nested-module grammar (`<repo>:<module-dir>`) and the new `--list` mode both parse the same file through separate awk readers. They agree today because someone checked by hand.

**Reproduction that belongs in the suite**, from the 2026-08-30 fix:

    replace ( // pin the local tree while migrating
        github.com/yasyf/leaked-by-the-bug v1.2.3 => ../leaked
    )

Before: `leaked-by-the-bug` printed as a requirement. After: it does not, while a plain block and a single-line `replace foo => bar` still behave.

Note the script's own header documents what it deliberately does not cover ("Not covered, by construction"); a test suite should assert those refusals too, not just the happy paths.</body>

ops.text: A Go test drives scripts/fleet-build.sh's refs-file parsing against fixture files, covering at minimum: --list emitting bare repo names for nested-module entries, --ref resolution, and check_refs refusing a refs-file/default_repos divergence
fleet_requires is covered against go.mod fixtures including a `replace ( // comment` block opener, a plain block, and a single-line replace
The suite runs in CI alongside the existing shell-driving suites
